newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Windsor Castle to reopen early after fire.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Windsor Castle to reopen early after fire.

text.p: Windsor Castle, Queen Elizabeth's home just outside London which was ravaged by a fire in 1992, is to reopen ahead of schedule at the start of next year, officials said on Tuesday.
The final phase of a 38 million pound ($64 million) restoration was launched when three giant oak columns were hoisted into place by a huge crane in the castle's Octagon anteroom.
The British monarch's favourite castle was badly damaged in November 1992 by a blaze that began in the private chapel and rapidly spread.

Royal collection spokesman Dickie Arbiter said the castle would be open to the public again from the start of 1998. "With the help of good contractors and architects, we are able to finish ahead of schedule," he told reporters.
He said 70 percent of the restoration funding came from opening Buckingham Palace, the royal residence in central London, to visitors and from charging admission to the grounds of Windsor Castle.
